_meta.note: PRE-EARNINGS PREVIEW. This is the first hard read on whether the Brent collapse (~$100 late-Jul -> $79.47 Aug-04) is actually reaching BAFS margins, or whether the pass-through lag defers it to H2. Figures below are house assumptions and structural reasoning, NOT company guidance and NOT sell-side consensus (no broker note on BAFS H1-2026 was retrievable at run time). Loaded by earnings_tracker.load_earnings_preview('BAFS.BK'). Replace with bafs_h12026_actual.json once results print.
_meta.why_this_matters_for_tho: BAFS is ~29% of the ex-gold portfolio and is the ONE holding that the Aug-04/05 oil regime change helps rather than hurts. PTTEP (~35%) is the mirror image. This print tells him whether the hedge is working.

price_context.read: The stock has ALREADY moved +5.9% on the oil relief before any reported evidence of it. That is the market pricing the input-cost read, not the earnings. Still deep in the lower half of a 6.70-17.60 range, so the recovery is early rather than stretched — but it does mean an in-line H1 is not automatically a positive catalyst.

structural_model.business: Jet-fuel storage, hydrant pipeline and into-plane refuelling at Suvarnabhumi/Don Mueang plus the Fuel Pipeline Transportation (FPT) network and a small renewable-power arm.
structural_model.revenue_driver: VOLUME (aircraft refuelled / litres throughput), not the fuel price itself — BAFS charges a SERVICE fee per unit, it does not take outright fuel-price risk on the core into-plane business.
structural_model.cost_driver: Energy and power costs, pipeline pumping cost, finance cost on the FPT capex, and D&A.
structural_model.oil_transmission_channel: INDIRECT and LAGGED. Lower jet fuel does not lift BAFS revenue per litre; it works through (a) airline economics -> more flights/frequency -> higher throughput volume, and (b) BAFS's own energy/pumping cost line. Channel (a) is the bigger one and takes 1-2 quarters to show in schedules.
structural_model.common_mistake_to_avoid: Treating BAFS as a short-oil proxy. It is a VOLUME/TOURISM proxy with a modest cost-side oil kicker. A cheap-oil quarter with weak arrivals is a BAD quarter for BAFS.

house_estimates.confidence: LOW — house reasoning only, no broker consensus retrievable at run time. Treat the bands as scenario framing, not forecasts.

h1_2026_revenue_direction.note: Driven by foreign-arrival throughput. Thailand's 2026 arrivals target is ~35.5m but the Jan-Nov 2025 run-rate CONTRACTED ~8% YoY, and the World Bank cut 2026 Thai growth to 1.6% partly on a slower tourism recovery. So volume is the risk, not the fuel price.

h1_2026_margin_direction.note: H1 = Jan-Jun 2026. Brent spent most of that window ELEVATED (the collapse to $79 only happened Aug-03/04). So the H1 print largely PRE-DATES the relief. Expect the oil benefit to show in H2/Q3-Q4, not in this report.

house_estimates.key_swing_factor: Foreign arrivals / flight frequency at Suvarnabhumi. A throughput beat matters far more than any input-cost line.

beat_on_volume.trigger: Throughput/refuelling volume up YoY with revenue growth >5%.
beat_on_volume.read: The genuinely bullish case — tourism recovery is real AND the oil relief is still to come in H2. This is the scenario in which the +5.9% move so far is under- rather than over-priced.
beat_on_volume.action_for_tho: Thesis strengthens. Still no chase — size is already ~29% of the ex-gold book.

in_line.trigger: Revenue flat, margin stable, no volume surprise.
in_line.read: MOST LIKELY. H1 pre-dates the oil collapse, so an in-line print is not a disappointment — it just means the catalyst is deferred to the Q3 print (Nov) and the Aug-28 investor meeting is where forward volume guidance matters.
in_line.action_for_tho: Hold. Do not read an in-line H1 as the oil thesis failing — check the Aug-28 meeting commentary on H2 throughput instead.

miss_on_volume.trigger: Throughput down YoY; revenue contraction; arrivals shortfall confirmed.
miss_on_volume.read: THE REAL RISK, and the one the +5.9% rally is not pricing. If arrivals are weak, cheap jet fuel does not save the quarter — it is a service-fee-per-litre business. Would also validate the World Bank's 1.6% Thai growth cut.
miss_on_volume.action_for_tho: Re-examine the position. This is the scenario that turns BAFS from 'the holding the oil regime change helps' into a tourism-cycle problem.

key_watch_items: Refuelling VOLUME / throughput YoY — the single most important line. Revenue growth without volume growth is just tariff mix.
Foreign arrival trend commentary — reconcile against the 35.5m 2026 target vs the ~8% YoY contraction seen through Jan-Nov 2025.
FPT (Fuel Pipeline Transportation) segment contribution and its finance cost / gearing — the capex drag on this arm has historically been the margin swing factor.
Any interim dividend declaration alongside H1 (BAFS trailing yield ~3.28%; a declaration would be a second-order positive).
Energy/power cost line — the only place the Brent collapse can show up directly in H1, and it will be small.
Management's H2 guidance at the CONFIRMED 2026-08-28 investor meeting — arguably more decision-relevant than the H1 numbers themselves.

oil_regime_context_2026_08_05.read: Brent has fallen ~20% from the late-July peak and printed its first sub-$80 of the conflict series. For BAFS this is unambiguously the right direction — but the transmission is lagged and indirect, so it should be expected in the Q3/Q4 prints and in airline scheduling decisions, NOT in this H1 report.
oil_regime_context_2026_08_05.two_sided_risk: The oil_scenario model still carries 24% combined weight on the two escalation tails ($105/$115) because Iran denies direct US talks, Rubio confirms no final agreement, and Trump framed the Aug-04 round as Iran's 'last chance'. A collapse of that round reverses the BAFS input-cost tailwind quickly.

advisory_note_for_tho: Set expectations correctly before Aug-14: H1-2026 covers Jan-Jun, a window in which Brent was mostly ELEVATED. The oil relief that pushed BAFS +5.9% happened in AUGUST and cannot be in these numbers. So judge this print on VOLUME (arrivals/throughput), not on margin, and treat the confirmed Aug-28 investor meeting as the more important event because that is where H2 guidance lands. The genuine risk to watch is not oil at all — it is Thai tourist arrivals, which contracted ~8% YoY through late 2025 and which the World Bank cited when cutting 2026 Thai growth to 1.6%. Informational, not a trade recommendation.
